The test image shows a corn leaf with a single elongated, narrow, pale yellow-to-tan lesion running parallel to the leaf veins. Key features: elongated, vein-parallel, pale/tan color, diffuse margins. Top candidates: Gray Leaf Spot (rectangular vein-bounded lesions), Northern Leaf Blight (cigar-shaped tan lesions), Stewart's Disease (streaky pale lesions).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

This Northern Leaf Blight reference (Corn_Disease_127) is a strong visual match — elongated, pale tan/white lesions running parallel to leaf veins on otherwise green leaves. The test image shows the same pattern at an earlier stage (more yellow-green margins, less complete necrosis), but the shape and distribution are consistent with NLB.
